solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Now and then, writer is in very British newspaper (9)

indicatorNotes.is in: the writer is placed in the words that follow, so its letters sit inside theirs

blocks.note: so = very, as in 'so good'
the writer of the clue refers to himself as me
The Times, a London daily

annotation.surface: A journalist occasionally gets a piece into a very British paper.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter is writing in The Times itself, so the clue is a small in-joke about its own contributors.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something that happens on occasion but not regularly.

entries.clue: Sacks revolutionary displaying foot in some fonts (5)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a turning round, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: to fire staff is to sack them

annotation.surface: A radical sacked from his job shows up in a typeface.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel; here it is an adjective telling you to turn FIRES round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the small stroke finishing a letter's stem sits at its base like a foot in typefaces such as Times.

entries.clue: Several notes from children still at church accepted by God squad at last (5,7,5)

indicatorNotes.accepted by: something accepted by a person is taken in, so the church abbreviation goes inside the god
indicatorNotes.at last: at the last means at the end, so only the final letter of squad is used

blocks.note: minors are people under age
even = still, as in 'even better'
Thor, the Norse god of thunder, split open to take the church abbreviation
CH = church
the last letter of squad

annotation.surface: Children still at church are welcomed by a band of keen evangelists and sing a few notes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'God squad' reads as one phrase, slang for keen evangelical Christians, but it splits: God is a Norse deity and squad only lends its final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a chord is several notes sounded together, and a minor seventh is one kind of chord.

entries.clue: Prime Minister once shortened concluding part of Riot Act, a legal document (5,4)

indicatorNotes.shortened: made shorter, so the name loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.concluding part of: the part that concludes a word is its end, its final letter

blocks.note: Liz Truss, briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022, cut short
the last letter of riot
a deed is an act

annotation.surface: A former Prime Minister cut short the reading of the Riot Act.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Riot Act' looks like one legal term, but it splits: Riot gives only its last letter and Act stands alone. Liz Truss's premiership lasted just 49 days, which suits 'shortened'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the document that creates a trust and names its trustees is one kind of legal deed.

entries.clue: Bodily strength of marine bivalve announced (6)

indicatorNotes.announced: what is announced is spoken aloud, so the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a mussel is a shellfish with two hinged shells, a bivalve

annotation.surface: Someone declares how strong a shellfish is.
annotation.walkthrough: MUSSEL and MUSCLE are said the same way, so the shellfish, spoken, gives the word for strength.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the tissue that moves the body stands for the strength it gives, as in 'put some muscle into it'.

entries.clue: Dad’s trusted to work with lots of famous people (4-7)

indicatorNotes.to work: letters put to work are set moving, and they settle in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange; the apostrophe is ignored

annotation.surface: Father is trusted to work alongside a lot of celebrities.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as Dad landing a job among celebrities; 'to work' is the instruction to rearrange his letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: stars are famous performers, and a cast studded with them is thick with celebrities.

entries.clue: Drank regularly eating German spicy dish (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
indicatorNotes.eating: whatever is eaten ends up inside, so the German goes into the kept letters

blocks.note: the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of drank
Hans, a typical German man's name

annotation.surface: Someone drank steadily while tucking into a spicy German dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'German spicy dish' reads as one phrase; the German is only a name, and the dish is Indian.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this Parsi curry of meat and lentils, usually hot and sour, is one kind of spicy dish.

entries.clue: Mafia bosses in singular academic positions (8)

blocks.note: a Mafia boss is a don
in = fashionable = hip
s = singular, the grammar abbreviation

annotation.surface: Mafia bosses are found in unusual university posts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing the bosses somewhere; it means fashionable. Don is also the Oxford and Cambridge word for a university teacher.
annotation.definitionFit: A formed word: -ship turns a role into the post held, so the posts of Oxbridge teachers, the other kind of don, are academic positions.

entries.clue: Founder of controversial website in, for example, Caribbean capital curtailed on returning (7)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: to curtail is literally to cut the tail, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.on returning: what returns comes back, and in a down answer the letters read back up the grid

blocks.note: e.g. = for example
Nassau, capital of the Bahamas, without its last letter

annotation.surface: The founder of a notorious website turns up in some Caribbean capital.
annotation.walkthrough: EG and the shortened capital are written in clue order, EGNASSA, and the whole string is then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Julian Assange founded WikiLeaks, the site that published leaked secret documents.

entries.clue: After Saturday, add sensible pottery (7,4)

blocks.note: Sat = Saturday
to sum is to add up
sensible in its older sense of conscious of, as in 'sensible of the danger'

annotation.surface: After Saturday, a practical kind of pottery gets added.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sensible' looks like 'practical'; it means aware, an older sense still found in 'sensible of'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this cream-glazed Japanese earthenware from Satsuma is one kind of pottery.

entries.clue: Travelling around USA with Amtrak for Hindu text (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Travelling around: letters travelling around move from place to place and end up in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A traveller crosses America by Amtrak with a religious book in hand.
annotation.walkthrough: Amtrak is the US national rail company, which makes the rail trip read naturally.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this ancient Sanskrit treatise on love and pleasure is a Hindu text.

entries.clue: Cold meat with side of potatoes is a winner (5)

indicatorNotes.side of: the side of a word is its edge, here its first letter

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
ham is a meat
the first letter of potatoes

annotation.surface: Cold meat with a side of potatoes makes a winning meal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a dinner, and CHAMP is also an Irish dish of mashed potato with spring onions.
annotation.definitionFit: A shortening: champ is informal for champion, whoever has won.

entries.clue: Sickness in slum in upward curve (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the slum is put in the curve, its letters inside
indicatorNotes.upward: in a down answer, going upward means reading from the bottom, so the curve is reversed

blocks.note: a hole is a squalid place to live
a curve is an arc, here read upwards

annotation.surface: Disease spreads through a slum on a rising curve of infection.
annotation.walkthrough: The word 'in' does two jobs: the first joins definition to wordplay, the second places the slum inside the curve.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this waterborne infection is one kind of sickness, and slums are where it spreads.

entries.clue: Clotheshorse is lighter, but fine to leave (5)

indicatorNotes.to leave: the F is told to leave, so it departs from the word

blocks.note: fairer = lighter in colour
F = fine, as on pencil grades; it is removed

annotation.surface: A vain dresser is paler now, but fine to go.
annotation.walkthrough: A clotheshorse is also a vain dresser, which the surface plays on; here it is the frame for drying laundry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name the folding frame on which washing is hung to dry.

entries.clue: Net contracts with one in Germany (5,5)

blocks.note: to purse the lips is to contract them
eine is German for one

annotation.surface: Net income and contracts are drawn up with a firm in Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Net' and 'contracts' suggest business; it is a fishing net and puckering lips.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this big fishing net, drawn shut at the bottom like a purse, is one kind of net.

entries.clue: Dismissals in heavy beatings entertaining a Parisian (7)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: a host entertaining a guest has it inside the house, so the beatings hold the French word

blocks.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
un is French for a; it goes inside after the R

annotation.surface: Players are sacked after heavy defeats, one of them hosting a Frenchman.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is run out when the ball breaks the wicket before he completes a run.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: in cricket this is one of the ways a batsman is dismissed.

entries.clue: Girl from the east disengaged somewhat (5)

indicatorNotes.from the east: in an across answer, east is the right-hand end, so read from right to left
indicatorNotes.somewhat: somewhat means to some extent, so only some of the word is used

blocks.note: the letters inside diSENGAged, to be read backwards

annotation.surface: A girl from the east has become somewhat detached.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From the east' sounds like where the girl comes from; it tells you to read right to left.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is a girl's name.

entries.clue: Embroiderer in open car nursing foot when I passed (9)

indicatorNotes.nursing: a nurse holds a baby close, so the car holds the foot inside
indicatorNotes.when I passed: the I has passed on, gone, so it is taken out

blocks.note: a tourer is an open-topped touring car
IAMB, a metrical foot, without its I; it goes inside the car after its first letter

annotation.surface: A needleworker drives an open-topped car, nursing a sore foot, just as I went by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is the poetic foot, not a body part: an iamb is one short beat and one long.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a tambour is a round frame holding fabric taut, and this is someone who embroiders on one.

entries.clue: Fantastic new atherosclerosis drugs blocking iron the result of years of hard work? (5-5,7,6)

annotation.definition: the result of years of hard work?

indicatorNotes.Fantastic: fantastic means wildly unreal, so the letters are made into something unrecognisable
indicatorNotes.blocking: the drugs block the iron by sitting inside it

blocks.note: N = new
used as it stands
Fe, the chemical symbol for iron, with the drugs inside it
used as it stands

annotation.surface: An exciting new treatment for hardened arteries blocks iron, the fruit of years of medical research.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a medical breakthrough; the long fodder is just letters to rearrange. The question mark admits the definition describes rather than defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the top British university grade is earned after years of study.

entries.clue: After revolution, sneakily look again for ideal partner (6)

indicatorNotes.After revolution: after a revolution, a half-turn, the letters face the other way and read backwards

blocks.note: re- = again
to peek is to look furtively

annotation.surface: After a revolution, someone sneaks another look at the perfect partner.
annotation.walkthrough: RE and PEEK join as REPEEK, 'look again', and the whole is then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: a partner worth holding on to for good is called one, as in 'she's a keeper'.

entries.clue: New Zealand parrot circling female author (5)

indicatorNotes.circling: to circle something is to go round it, so the parrot surrounds the letter

blocks.note: the kaka is a large New Zealand parrot
F = female

annotation.surface: A New Zealand parrot flies round a woman writer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Female author' reads as one phrase, but the female is only the F and the author is a man.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Franz Kafka wrote The Trial and Metamorphosis.

entries.clue: Order mixed bean soup (8)

indicatorNotes.mixed: things that are mixed are stirred together, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A diner orders a bowl of mixed bean soup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a verb for asking for food; it is a noun, a court order.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this writ commanding a witness to attend court is one kind of legal order.

entries.clue: A long walk, or wild parties? (7)

indicatorNotes.wild: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone must choose between a long hike and some riotous parties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like it offers two definitions; the second half is wordplay, and the question mark hints at it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a noun: a tiring, trudging walk.

entries.clue: I’m not sure chap with English books welcomed by Trump, say, is legal immigrant (9,8)

indicatorNotes.welcomed by: a guest welcomed by a host is taken in, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: er, the sound of hesitation
a chap is a man
E = English
NT = New Testament, a set of books
Donald Trump is an example of a president; the other letters go in after the P

annotation.surface: An uncertain man with English books is welcomed by Trump, apparently as a lawful immigrant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Trump as one example of a president.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: an immigrant granted the lawful right to live in a country indefinitely holds this status.

entries.clue: Fast horses live here (6)

blocks.note: fast = firmly fixed, as in 'stuck fast'
the building where horses are housed

annotation.surface: Racehorses are kept here.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast horses' reads as racehorses; fast is a separate definition meaning firm.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective, steady and firmly fixed, and a noun, the building horses are kept in.

entries.clue: Department boss with unknown research project (5,5)

blocks.note: a field is an area of study, a department
a boss is a raised knob, a stud
y, an algebraic unknown

annotation.surface: A head of department takes on a research project with an unknown outcome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Department boss' reads as one person; boss here is a knob or stud, as on a shield.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: research done on site, in the field, rather than in a lab is one kind of research project.

entries.clue: Moderate plonk with Adam and Eva? (3,1,6,2)

blocks.note: to plonk something down is to put it
used as it stands
Eva Perón, Argentina's first lady

annotation.surface: A modest amount of cheap wine is shared by Adam and Eve.
annotation.walkthrough: Plonk is British for cheap wine, and 'Eva' is easily read as Eve beside Adam, but she is Eva Perón.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a damper checks a fire's draught, so to fit one is to hold something back, to moderate it.

entries.clue: University rector stopping home in trouble (6)

indicatorNotes.stopping: a stopper plugs a hole, so the rector sits inside the home

blocks.note: U = university
a nest is a home
R = rector; it goes inside the home

annotation.surface: A university rector is blocking someone's home while in difficulties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' reads as calling at a house; it means plugging, so R goes inside NEST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: public disturbance or discontent is trouble.

entries.clue: Destination of couples, with romance primarily promoted? (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means in the first place, so only the first letter
indicatorNotes.promoted: someone promoted moves up a rank, so the R moves up one place

blocks.note: pairs are couples
the first letter of romance; it moves up past the I

annotation.surface: Couples, romance to the fore, head for a destination.
annotation.walkthrough: The destination is apt: this capital is the classic romantic trip for couples, which the question mark acknowledges.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the French capital is a destination, and famously one for couples.

entries.clue: One’s fired priest over the phone (6)

annotation.definitionNote: 'One's fired' means 'one is fired', a thing that gets fired

indicatorNotes.over the phone: what comes over the phone is only heard, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a canon is a priest attached to a cathedral

annotation.surface: Someone learns by phone that the priest has been sacked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fired' reads as dismissed from a job; it means shot, as a gun is. CANON and CANNON are said the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a big gun is a thing that is fired.

entries.clue: A long letter (5)

blocks.note: used as it stands
to long for something is to itch for it

annotation.surface: Someone has written a lengthy letter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A long letter' reads as a lengthy piece of mail; long is a verb, to yearn.
annotation.definitionFit: A spelt-out name: this is how the letter H is written as a word.

entries.clue: Welcome to round island nation (5)

indicatorNotes.to round: to round something is to go round it, so the greeting surrounds the island

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
an ait is a small island in a river, a British word

annotation.surface: A welcome is extended to an island nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island nation' reads as one phrase; the island gives AIT and the nation alone is the definition, though the answer is an island nation too.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Caribbean republic is a nation.

entries.clue: Seem likely, in auction? (3,4)

blocks.note: an old idiom, as in 'it bids fair to rain'
at an auction you might make a reasonable offer; the question mark flags the literal reading

annotation.surface: Something looks probable at a sale.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is read twice: the idiom meaning seem likely, and literally what a reasonable buyer does at an auction.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an idiom for seeming likely to happen, and, taken literally, making a fair offer at a sale.

entries.clue: Outside, by boring 90s girl group (8)

indicatorNotes.boring: boring means drilling into, so the X is driven inside the group's name

blocks.note: Eternal, a British girl band of the 1990s
x = by, as in 3 x 4, three by four; it goes inside after the E

annotation.surface: Someone finds a 90s girl group tedious from the outside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like 'dull'; it means drilling into.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe what lies on the outer side.

entries.clue: Youngster briefly under bottom of boat crossing River Test (3,3)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, the word is cut short by its last letter
indicatorNotes.under: in a down answer, what is under comes below, so the youngster goes last
indicatorNotes.bottom of: in a down clue, the bottom of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of boat
R = river
YOUTH without its last letter

annotation.surface: A youngster sits in the bottom of a boat crossing the River Test.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River Test' reads as the Hampshire trout river; the river gives only R and Test is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a noun: a trial run to see whether something or someone works.

entries.clue: America converted into oligarchy, principally, in tragedy for the West (8)

indicatorNotes.converted into: one thing converted into another becomes it, so the A turns into O
indicatorNotes.principally: principally means first of all, so only the first letter

blocks.note: an accident is a tragedy
A = America; this A is swapped out
the first letter of oligarchy; it replaces the A

annotation.surface: America's slide into rule by a few rich men is a tragedy for the West.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as political commentary; America is just the A of ACCIDENT, and oligarchy gives only its O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the western world, as opposed to the Orient.

entries.clue: Beneficially, name European after amphibious vehicle, as it were? (2,9)

blocks.note: a toad is an amphibian
a van is a vehicle
a tag is a name
E = European

annotation.surface: Someone profits by naming a European after an amphibious vehicle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As it were' admits the stretch: a toad van would be amphibious only in the sense that a toad is an amphibian.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to show something to advantage is to show it beneficially, in a favourable light.

entries.clue: Recalled an excursion via Hooters? (7)

indicatorNotes.Recalled: called back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: an, read backwards
a sally is a trip out

annotation.surface: Someone remembers a trip to Hooters, the American restaurant chain.
annotation.walkthrough: Hooter is British slang for nose, so 'via hooters' means through the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: sound produced through the nose, and hooters are noses.

entries.clue: According to Spooner, suspicion of Dawn in direct view (4,2,5)

indicatorNotes.According to Spooner: Rev. Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a suspicion is a sign of something; it takes the L sound from the dawn word
used as it stands
dawn is first light; it takes the S sound from the first word

annotation.surface: Spooner suspects a woman called Dawn is in plain view.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name; it is daybreak, first light.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the straight path from the eye to what it sees is a direct view.

entries.clue: Page three’s dropping resistance to change (5)

indicatorNotes.dropping: the word drops the R, letting it fall away
indicatorNotes.to change: letters that change swap places into a new order

blocks.note: the word with its S
R = resistance in physics; removed, leaving THEES

annotation.surface: Page three is losing its resistance to change.
annotation.walkthrough: Page Three was The Sun newspaper's topless-model page, dropped in 2015, which the surface nods to.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a single leaf of paper.

entries.clue: Part of body initially treated roughly (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of treated
'or so' means roughly, as in 'ten or so'

annotation.surface: Part of the body was at first handled roughly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' looks like harshly, describing the treatment; it means approximately.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the trunk, without head or limbs, is one part of the body.

entries.clue: Partly scrag Greg, a torchbearer for company that collates financial details (10)

indicatorNotes.Partly: partly means in part, so only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of scrag to the start of torchbearer

annotation.surface: Someone half-throttles Greg, a torchbearer, on behalf of a financial firm.
annotation.walkthrough: To scrag someone is British slang for grabbing or throttling them by the neck.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a website or firm that gathers prices and financial data from many sources into one place.

entries.clue: Early issues — flight into work restricted by particles of sand? (7,5)

indicatorNotes.into: the flight goes into the work, its letters inside
indicatorNotes.restricted by: hemmed in by the grains, so everything else sits inside them

blocks.note: op = opus, a work
a bird on the wing is in flight; it goes inside OP
grains of sand; the rest goes inside after GR

annotation.surface: A new business has teething troubles, its flight into work held up by sand.
annotation.walkthrough: The sand stopping a flight suggests a grounded plane; the particles are simply grains, and the question mark nods to the loose fit.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the aches of children's growth stand for the difficulties of any venture's early stages.

entries.clue: Lass doing badly quickly played notes (9)

indicatorNotes.badly: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A girl performing poorly rushes through her notes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a nervous music pupil; 'doing' is fodder, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a rapid slide up or down a run of notes.

entries.clue: Up-to-date question by guest throwing very harsh interrogator (10)

indicatorNotes.throwing: to throw something is to cast it away, so the guest discards the V

blocks.note: in = fashionable, current
qu. = question
a visitor is a guest
V = very; it is thrown out of the guest

annotation.surface: A trendy question from a guest throws off a very tough questioner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throwing' looks like 'disconcerting'; it means casting off a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: one who questions relentlessly, after the officers of the Inquisition.

entries.clue: All it takes, on reflection, to ignore king a fraction (9)

indicatorNotes.on reflection: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the letters are read backwards
indicatorNotes.to ignore: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the K goes

blocks.note: used as it stands
used as it stands
to nick is to take or steal
K = king, as in chess; dropped, leaving NICS

annotation.surface: Thinking it over, all you need to overlook the king is a small fraction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All it takes' reads as a stock phrase; takes is a separate verb meaning nicks. ALL IT NICS is then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tiny trace or amount, from the Latin for spark.

entries.clue: Spike organised introduction to trainspotting — very harrowing (8)

indicatorNotes.introduction to: the introduction comes first, so the first letter

blocks.note: to spike a drink is to lace it
to run an event is to organise it
the first letter of trainspotting

annotation.surface: Spike planned an opening to trainspotting that turned out very distressing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spike organised' reads as a man doing the organising, and 'organised' looks like an anagram signal; it is RAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: lacerating means tearing flesh, so feelings torn this way are harrowed.

entries.clue: After being snubbed, impolite of setter to detain large dynasty’s founder (6,1)

indicatorNotes.After being snubbed: a snub nose is short, so the word is cut short by its last letter
indicatorNotes.to detain: to detain someone is to hold them in, so OF holds the L

blocks.note: rude = impolite; snubbed, it loses its E
used as it stands, with L inside
L = large
the setter calls himself I

annotation.surface: After being snubbed, a rude crossword setter holds up the founder of a great dynasty.
annotation.walkthrough: Snubbed looks like 'ignored'; it means cut short, as a snub nose is.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Habsburg count, elected King of the Romans in 1273, founded the dynasty's power.

entries.clue: Star with nothing boosted American footballer (7)

indicatorNotes.boosted: what is boosted is pushed up, and in a down answer that means reading from the bottom

blocks.note: a big name is a star
nil = nothing

annotation.surface: A star player boosted from nothing becomes an American footballer.
annotation.walkthrough: NAME and NIL join in clue order, then the whole is read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a player on the line of scrimmage is one kind of American footballer.

entries.clue: Curry and French wine with Father John (8)

blocks.note: vin is French for wine
da = dad, father
john is American slang for a toilet, as is British loo

annotation.surface: A priest named John has a curry and French wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Father John' reads as a priest; the two words split, and john is slang for a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this fiery Goan dish is one kind of curry.

entries.clue: Terrible encores cause death (7)

indicatorNotes.Terrible: something terrible is in an awful state, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Awful encores are the death of a show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cause death' reads as a comic exaggeration about bad performances; it is the definition, a medical verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: in medicine the verb means to make body tissue die, or to die.

entries.clue: Person eating in restaurant with love for American bread (6)

blocks.note: someone eating out
love = zero, O, in tennis scoring

annotation.surface: A diner in a restaurant, with love, asks for American bread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' reads as food, fitting the restaurant; it is slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: Spanish for money, borrowed into American slang, just as bread is slang for cash.

entries.clue: Mystery in game resolved (6)

indicatorNotes.resolved: resolved means broken down and set out again, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A mystery in a game is finally solved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word; it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something puzzling or hard to explain.

entries.clue: Add pounds to pot when playing card game, reportedly, and panic (3,4,8,2,1,5)

annotation.answer: GET ONE'S KNICKERS IN A TWIST

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the phrase is judged by its sound

blocks.clueFragment: Add pounds to pot when playing card game
blocks.soundsLike: GET ONE'S NICKERS IN A TWIST
blocks.note: nicker is British slang for a pound; you put your pounds in the pot when you twist, taking another card in pontoon

annotation.surface: A card player puts more money in the pot and then loses their nerve.
annotation.walkthrough: Knickers are British for women's underpants, and 'nicker' is slang for a pound, so the two sound alike. In pontoon, a British card game, 'twist' asks for another card.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: British slang for getting flustered and upset over something minor.

entries.clue: Recording short, easy putt (3-2)

indicatorNotes.short: a word that is short falls short of its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: taping is recording, and it loses its G

annotation.surface: A golfer films a short, easy putt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short, easy putt' reads as one description; short belongs with recording and cuts it.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a putt so close to the hole that it needs only a tap.

entries.clue: Not one retailer stocks chemical for photocopier (5)

indicatorNotes.stocks: a shop that stocks something holds it inside, so the words hold the answer

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of not to the start of retailer

annotation.surface: No shop stocks the powder a photocopier needs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stocks' looks like a shop's inventory, fitting the retailer; it is the hiding instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the powdered ink a photocopier fuses onto paper.

entries.clue: Obsessive desire to publish in mostly kind country having run away (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.having run away: the R for run has run away, leaving the word

blocks.note: TYPE, a kind, without its last letter
the European country
R = run, as in cricket scoring; it leaves the country

annotation.surface: A compulsive writer craves to publish in a kinder country, after fleeing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run away' reads as fleeing; it tells you R has gone from ROMANIA.
annotation.definitionFit: A formed word: -mania is a craze, and typo- means type, so a craze for seeing oneself in print.

entries.clue: Japanese coin found in Argyll and Bute town close to Clachaig (5)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter

blocks.note: Oban, a port town on the west coast of Scotland
the last letter of Clachaig

annotation.surface: A Japanese coin turns up in a Scottish town near Clachaig.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near, and Clachaig is a real place in Argyll; it means the close, or end, of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this large oval gold piece of old Japan is a coin.

entries.clue: Ship is grand the whole time (7)

blocks.note: G = grand, a thousand pounds
all = the whole
an eon is a long time

annotation.surface: A ship is looking grand all the time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The whole time' reads as one phrase meaning always, and 'grand' as splendid; a grand is slang for a thousand pounds.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the big square-rigged sailing vessel of Spain's treasure fleets is one kind of ship.

entries.clue: Fight arrest (3,2)

blocks.note: a quarrel or clash, as in 'a brush with the law'
police slang for taking a suspect to the station

annotation.surface: Someone resists arrest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fight arrest' reads as resisting the police; the two words are separate definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a noun for a clash or quarrel, and a phrasal verb for taking someone into custody.

entries.clue: Scoff too much? Partner scratching head before repast, off and on (7)

indicatorNotes.scratching head: to scratch something out is to strike it, so the head, the first letter, goes
indicatorNotes.off and on: off and on means intermittently, so letters are skipped and kept in turn

blocks.note: LOVER without its first letter
the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of repast

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether they eat too much, while their partner scratches their head over a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' reads as mock; it is British slang for eating greedily.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: scoff means gobble, so doing it to excess is eating too much.

entries.clue: I rate Chas & Dave finally breaking rubbish flower (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is what this taster might say of the job: cha is slang for tea

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so the last letter
indicatorNotes.breaking: the E breaks into the rubbish, sitting inside it

blocks.note: tat is junk
the last letter of Dave; it breaks into the rubbish
an aster is a daisy-like flower

annotation.surface: A fan rates the Cockney duo Chas & Dave, while calling their flowers rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: Chas & Dave were a Cockney pop duo; 'Chas' here is the plural of cha, slang for tea, so the whole of 'I rate Chas' is what a tea taster says.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: someone paid to grade teas could say 'I rate chas'.
